newsitem.title: PERU: AEI boss warns on LatAm growth constraints.
newsitem.headline: AEI boss warns on LatAm growth constraints.

text.p: Latin American won't realize its full potential as a global air cargo centre until it modernizes its infrastructure, security and technology, the head of Air Express International told delegates at the ALACAT congress and exhibition.
Gunther Rohrman, chief executive of the U.S. freight forwarder, said economic liberalization in many Latin American countries has spurred the growth of trade, but not made it more efficient.

He called on Latin American governments to embrace a spate of measures, such as negotiating open skies agreements with the United States. He also called for more private sector investment to improve infrastructure expansion and modernization.
Rohrmann's remarks were summarized in a statement issued by AEI.
In his speech, Rohrmann signalled several ways in which Latin American governments are constraining the growth of air freight.
Customs clearance regulations are "inefficient and punitive" and lead to excessive delays in releasing cargo, he said.
Currently, only Chile and Costa Rica have customs systems that measure up to the rest of the world, he added.
There is excessive theft of goods.
Many Latin American ports are overcrowded, and the road network is inadequate, he said.

Rohrmann criticized what he said is the "tightly controlled" markets for aviation services and the inability of Latin American airlines to develop automated systems to transmit shipment information electronically.

What is needed is "a world-class infrastructure, world-class information technology and an increased emphasis on security", he said, adding that increased privatisation of infrastructure would assure an adequate supply of capital to modernize the port, airport and road systems.
Customs authorities should cease levying penalties for routine paperwork errors, he said.

In Argentina, a misdeclaration can generate fines up to twice the value of the goods, he said, adding that Latin American governments must invest in systems to clear goods while they are still en route, and they must keep the customs apparatus operating 24 hours a day. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017 - www.racs.com
